title: How To Build Rapport When You Have A Quiet Personality
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin reassures introverted teachers that building rapport requires no verbal gift or outgoing personality. He argues that proactively trying to draw students out actually makes many uncomfortable, and that the strongest rapport instead forms when students come to the teacher on their own terms. His prescription is deceptively simple: be consistently pleasant in every interaction, especially in front of the whole class, and let the Law of Reciprocity do the rest. Because students feel no pressure and no ulterior motive from a teacher who's simply good-natured, they gravitate toward that teacher naturally, and even students who never initiate conversation still feel connected to a consistently kind teacher. He frames this as advice usable by anyone, quiet or extroverted, first-year or veteran, since it was a founding SCM principle never to recommend a strategy that not every teacher could do.
points: Proactively trying to draw out shy or quiet students can make many of them uncomfortable rather than building genuine rapport.
The strongest rapport forms when students come to the teacher voluntarily rather than the teacher pursuing conversation.
Being consistently pleasant in every interaction, especially in front of the whole class, is the one method that works for any personality type.
The Law of Reciprocity means students feel connected to a consistently kind teacher even without frequent personal conversation.
This approach requires no invented persona, interview-style questioning, or mimicking of student behavior — just steady good nature.
quotes: It’s easy to admire teachers with the gift of gab, high social IQ, and ability to build rapport so quickly.
With the right approach, you never have to do anything or be anything you’re not in order to build strong, influential rapport with your students.
The highest level of rapport between you and your students happens when they come to you . It’s when they’re drawn to you.

If you’re a regular reader of SCM, then you know it’s to simply be consistently pleasant. Be good natured in all your dealings with students, especially when in front of the entire class, and rapport develops organically.
You just have to be pleasant and they’ll come to you. And when they come to you, conversation is natural and effortless.
The Law of Reciprocity is so strong and predictable that although you may not know some of your students well, at least on a personal, non-academic level, they’ll feel like they know you.
